where: scripts/qa-implicit-submit.mjs (the whole drive) and scripts/implicit-submit.test.mts §2 (enterSubmits, the engine model)
problem: No real browser proves the WebKit and Firefox halves of the pre-hydration seal. The drive launches chromium only. In Chromium the disabled default button alone stops implicit submission, so P1 and P2 stay green even if the hidden second text field is deleted. The drive therefore gives zero evidence for the only thing protecting iPhones (the second text field), and none for Gecko's default-button rule. Both rest solely on enterSubmits(), a model the same author wrote from a reading of each engine's source. That model is already wrong for a shipped WebKit (see the next problem). On a money path, the iPhone claim 'before the page wakes Enter submits nothing' is unrun.
evidence: qa-implicit-submit.mjs: `import { chromium } from "playwright"` is the only engine. The draft's own last driveCase says 'NOT DRIVEN ... WebKit and Firefox'. Checked: WebKit main and Gecko MaybeSubmitForm match the model today, so the claim is probably true. But WebKit's safari-7614-branch submitImplicitly differs from main (renderer check), and the model encodes main only.
fix: Parametrize the drive by engine: ENGINE=chromium|webkit|firefox → playwright[ENGINE].launch(); Playwright ships all three on Windows. Run at least P1, P2, W1 and C1 under webkit and firefox. Run the red control on the pre-A8j tree per engine: P1 must go red in all three (a native POST that withdraws) and green after. Add a webkit-only control with the second field planted out in memory, e.g. by page.route rewriting the HTML to drop the unnamed hidden text input; P1 must then go red in WebKit. That proves the field, not the model. Keep the drive outside predeploy.

where: src/components/ui/confirm-dialog.tsx (the hidden default <button ... hidden ...>), and the claims in the submitsForm prop doc, the summary and check 2.2
problem: On iOS/iPadOS Safari 16.0–16.3, after hydration, Enter in the amount box or the phrase box does NOTHING: no dialog. WebKit's implicit submission clicks a successful submit button there only if it has a renderer, and a `hidden` (display:none) button has none. It is not counted either, and the two text fields block a plain submit. This is money-safe: nothing submits before or after hydration. But these claims are false on those builds: 'Enter in such a form opens the dialog ... before the page wakes, while it hydrates and after', 'once it listens Enter submits in all three', and 2.2's WebKit branch. So the gate would pin a behaviour a real iPhone does not have.
evidence: WebKit safari-7614-branch (Safari 16.0–16.3), HTMLFormElement::submitImplicitly: `if (formElement.isSuccessfulSubmitButton()) { if (formElement.renderer()) { formElement.dispatchSimulatedClick(&event); return; } } else if (formElement.canTriggerImplicitSubmission()) ++submissionTriggerCount;`. safari-7615-branch, safari-7616/7618 and main drop the renderer() check. That matches the draft's model.
fix: Option 1: correct the prop doc, the notes and the 2.2 label to 'WebKit from Safari 16.4'. Record that on 16.0–16.3 Enter in these forms is inert (safe), and extend enterSubmits with a webkit-legacy variant that skips non-rendered submit buttons. Option 2, if Enter must open the dialog there too: draw the default control rendered but invisible (zero-size, clipped, aria-hidden, tabIndex -1) instead of `hidden`, and model the renderer rule.

where: src/components/ui/confirm-dialog.tsx, formGuard().listen (the onSubmit that always calls refused())
problem: A held Enter in a guarded field calls refused() on every auto-repeat. (a) With an invalid amount, each repeat runs requestOpen → openGuard → a new kit warning toast, about 30 a second. toast.tsx holds overflow rather than dropping it, and paints each held toast later with its full dwell, so a 1–2 s hold queues dozens of identical warnings plus haptics for a minute or more. This is new on every field of the withdraw and deposit forms: deposit's Enter did nothing before. (b) Suppose the dialog was opened from the field and Enter is held on Cancel or 'Keep my account'. The press closes the dialog, Modal returns focus to the field (restoreTo is the element focused at open), the next repeat implicitly submits, the guard refuses it, and the dialog reopens. That is the K defect (held-key-stops-at-close-reopens-confirm) now reaching through the amount and phrase boxes. Neither the notes nor the drive record it. No money moves: it reopens on Cancel.
evidence: Draft listen(): `if (confirming) return; e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); refused();`, with no look at the key. refuseRef is set to requestOpen whenever the dialog is closed and enabled. withdraw-confirm.tsx:96-105 and deposit-confirm.tsx:81-90: guardOpen toasts on every refusal. toast.tsx:178-187 present() always stacks; :284-316 overflow is held, not dropped; no groupKey on these toasts. modal.tsx:276-279 and :313: focus is restored to the element focused at open. held-key.ts:12-13 already says Enter in a field 'submits the form of a focused field'.
fix: In formGuard().listen, also add a capture-phase keydown listener on the form: `if (swallowsHeldKey(e.key, e.repeat, keyTargetOf(e.target))) e.preventDefault();`, reusing held-key.ts. Cancelling a repeat's keydown cancels its keypress, so no implicit submission, no refusal, no toast and no reopen. It also stops a held Enter on the trigger (it is inside the form) from reopening the dialog in these five forms. Remove it in the same stop(). Add a §1 probe: a repeat Enter keydown on an input in the form is cancelled, a fresh one is not, a textarea is untouched. Add a plant, and drive cases: '5' typed, Enter held 1 s → at most one toast; dialog opened by Enter, Enter held on Cancel → the dialog stays closed.

where: src/components/ui/confirm-dialog.tsx (formGuard created per dialog via guardRef) and check 1.5
problem: Two submitsForm dialogs in one form deadlock each other. Each guard refuses every submit outside its OWN confirm, and stopPropagation does not stop the other listener on the same form. So Enter opens BOTH dialogs. Dialog A's confirm calls requestSubmit; A's guard passes, B's guard prevents and stops the submit, so React never sees it, and B's refusal opens dialog B. A's commit never runs. Nothing in the prop doc, the census or 1.5 rules this out: 1.5 tests two guards on two DIFFERENT forms only. Latent: no form has two today. It is the obvious shape for a second confirm on the deposit or withdraw form, or for both RG confirms in one form.
evidence: Draft: `const guardRef = React.useRef<FormGuard | null>(null); if (guardRef.current === null) guardRef.current = formGuard();`, one `confirming` flag per dialog. Each listen() does `form.addEventListener("submit", onSubmit)` on the same form. Check 1.5 uses `const a = new EventTarget(); const b = new EventTarget();`.
fix: Make it impossible rather than silent. Keep a module-level WeakMap<HTMLFormElement, true> of guarded forms. A second dialog that tries to listen on an already-guarded form throws in development and console.errors in production, and does not enable its default button. Add a census rule (at most one submitsForm dialog per form-hosting component), a 1.5b probe with two guards on ONE target, and a plant.

where: scripts/implicit-submit.test.mts §4 (rule 4.1 via submissionsIn/reach), with formGuard().confirm in confirm-dialog.tsx
problem: Rule 4.1 demands submitsForm on any confirm whose reach contains requestSubmit()/submit(), wherever the call sits. But the guard passes only a submit fired synchronously inside confirm(). A confirm that submits after an await, a .then or a timer is forced by the gate into a configuration that can never send. In classic mode the deferred submit is refused as Enter's and the dialog reopens. In hold-open mode the Promise counts as 'started', so the dialog sets awaiting and shows a spinner, the deferred submit is refused, and pending never rises. The dialog then spins forever and cannot be dismissed (loading blocks scrim, Esc and the close button). The gate stays green. Latent: today's five are synchronous. The prop doc states the rule, but nothing checks it.
evidence: Draft formGuard.confirm: `confirming = true; try { return act(); } finally { confirming = false; }`. ConfirmDialog hold-open: `const started = guard.confirm(onConfirm); if (started === false) {...} setAwaiting(true);`, where a Promise is not false. submissionsIn() walks the whole function including nested closures, and 4.1 checks only presence.
fix: In the census, for a submitsForm dialog, require that the requestSubmit/submit call is reached without crossing a nested function boundary or an await/yield. A call inside an arrow passed to .then, setTimeout or startTransition, or after an await, FAILS with its location. Add a plant (an async onConfirm with submitsForm on the RG copy). Optionally, in development, console.error when confirm()'s act returns a thenable.

problem: The census fails OPEN on two shapes that leave Enter able to bypass a confirm. (1) A ConfirmDialog sits in a `<form action={x}>` and its onConfirm commits by calling the action itself, e.g. `startTransition(() => x(new FormData(formRef.current!)))`. (2) It submits through a helper imported from src/lib, e.g. `submitClosestForm(btn)`. submissionsIn sees no requestSubmit/submit member call, reach() does not follow imports, and 4.3 reads only `<form onSubmit>` (such a form has none). So the dialog is classed as 'does not submit', needs no submitsForm, and 4.0–4.4 stay green. Meanwhile Enter in a one-text-field form runs x with no confirm, which is exactly the A8j defect. The summary says the census 'fails closed', but that holds only for resolving the handler, not for what the handler's callees do. Latent: none today.
evidence: Draft: `const SUBMIT_CALLS = new Set(["requestSubmit", "submit"])`; submissionsIn requires `ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(n.expression)`. reach() follows only `ts.isIdentifier(n.expression)` callees whose binding fnOf() resolves to a function in the same file; an ImportSpecifier gives null. censusOfFile collects forms only `if (attrExpr(attrOf(t, "onSubmit")))`.
fix: In a confirm's reach, treat any call to an imported function as UNREAD (failing 4.0) unless it is on a short named allowlist (toast, router, haptics, ...). Add a rule: a `<form action={X}>` whose file renders a ConfirmDialog/ConfirmModal reaching X (by name) must carry submitsForm or be ledgered. Add both shapes to fixtureCensus and add plants.

where: src/components/ui/confirm-dialog.tsx, the hidden default `<button ref={defaultRef} type="submit" ... disabled={!listening} ...>`
problem: Firefox restores this button ENABLED before hydration on a reload or a history traversal that re-parses the page, which is exactly the window part (b) exists for. Gecko saves a button's disabled state once script has changed it; React removes `disabled` when the guard listens. On restore Gecko calls SetDisabled(false) while parsing. Enter in the amount box before hydration would then click the enabled default button: a native POST of withdrawAction or closeAccountAction, with no confirm. This is safe today only because Gecko discards layout state for no-store responses and Next serves these dynamic pages no-store. Any change that loses no-store on /wallet/withdraw, /wallet/deposit or /profile/account, or a submitsForm form on a static page, reopens the hole silently. No check pins it.
evidence: Gecko dom/html/HTMLButtonElement.cpp: SaveState `if (!mDisabledChanged) return; ... state->disabled() = HasAttr(nsGkAtoms::disabled); state->disabledSet() = true;`; RestoreState `if (aState && aState->disabledSet() && !aState->disabled()) { SetDisabled(false, IgnoreErrors()); }`. nsDocShell::ShouldDiscardLayoutState returns aChannel->IsNoStoreResponse. next.config.ts headers() sets Cache-Control only for static assets.
fix: Opt the control out of Gecko form-state restoration with autocomplete=off: Gecko then generates no state key, so nothing is saved or restored. @types/react types autoComplete on input, not on button, so draw it as `<input type="submit" ref={defaultRef} hidden disabled={!listening} formNoValidate tabIndex={-1} aria-hidden autoComplete="off" />`. Pin `autocomplete="off"` on the default control in check 2.3 with a plant, and update 3.3/3.4 to find an input type=submit.

where: scripts/qa-implicit-submit.mjs, asleep() and its callers P1 and P2
problem: The page with scripts held back is opened inside asleep(), but the try/finally that closes it starts only after asleep() returns. If p.goto or box.waitFor (90 s) throws during setup, runCase records a FAIL and the page stays open, with every .js request still aborted by its route. This is harmless to the later cases (each one uses the main page or opens a fresh one), but it does leak a page. This is the only mechanical defect found in the whole change set.
evidence: asleep(): const p = await ctx.newPage(); await p.route(...abort); await p.goto(...); await box.waitFor({ state: "visible", timeout: 90000 }); return { p, box, posts }; and in P1/P2: const { p, box, posts } = await asleep(...); try { ... } finally { await p.close(); }. A throw inside asleep() never reaches that finally.
fix: Inside asleep(), wrap the goto and the waitFor in try { ... } catch (e) { await p.close(); throw e; }. Or have asleep() return only after it registers p for closing in the caller's finally.

where: scripts/implicit-submit.test.mts §2 and §4.1 (how each form is proven), and the drive cases W1, D1, C1, P1 and P2
problem: No check proves that any real form blocks implicit submission. §4.1 only proves that the five dialogs carry `submitsForm`, and §2 renders a made-up `<form><input/>{dialog}</form>`. The fix only works while two things stay true: (a) the dialog sits inside the form its confirm submits, and (b) no submit control comes before the guard's default button in that form. Nothing checks either. The withdraw, deposit and RG forms are in page files the census never opens. The task asks for every form to be proven to block implicit submission; as written, a regression in a real form leaves the gate green.
evidence: §2 only draws `h("form", null, ...fields(n), dialog(true))`. §4.1 sets `guarded = isOn(attrOf(t, "submitsForm"))`. `censusOfFile` collects forms only from files that contain a dialog tag, so it never reads src/app/wallet/withdraw/page.tsx:222-296, src/app/wallet/deposit/page.tsx:219-288 or src/app/profile/responsible-gambling/page.tsx:208-218 and :236-246. The kit `<Button>` (src/components/ui/button.tsx:65-83) spreads `...rest` onto `<button>` and sets no default type, so inside a form it is a submit button. Chromium's `HTMLFormElement::SubmitImplicitly` (I checked chromium main) clicks the FIRST submit control in tree order when it is enabled. So if someone later adds `<Button onClick={...}>Max</Button>` above `<WithdrawConfirm>`, Enter before hydration posts `withdrawAction` natively with no confirm. After hydration the guard refuses it, but before hydration nothing does. test:implicit-submit stays green. Only P1 would notice, and that drive is outside predeploy.
fix: Add §4.5 THE HOSTS, listed by name: { withdraw/page.tsx, form `action={withdrawAction}`, `WithdrawConfirm` }, { deposit/page.tsx, `depositAction`, `DepositConfirm` }, { profile/responsible-gambling/page.tsx, `coolOffAction` and `selfExcludeAction`, `RgConfirmSubmit` }, { close-account-form.tsx, `closeAccountAction`, `ConfirmDialog` }, { sign-out-row.tsx, `"/auth/logout"`, `ConfirmDialog` }. For each, parse the host form's JSX and require: (1) the consumer sits inside the form; (2) nothing before it in source order can submit: no intrinsic `button` or kit `Button` without `type="button"`, no `SubmitButton`, no `input` of type submit or image. Also require that every use site of `WithdrawConfirm`, `DepositConfirm` and `RgConfirmSubmit` in src is a listed host. Plant: in withdraw/page.tsx change `"        {canSubmit ? <WithdrawConfirm"` (unique) to `"        <button>Max</button>{canSubmit ? <WithdrawConfirm"`, expecting 4.5. In the drive, after `fresh()` in W1, D1 and C1, and on the asleep page in P1 and P2, assert in the page that the first submit control of the box's form (in `form.elements` order) is the hidden guard button.

problem: The two exemptions are checked by text order: the opener's text must come before the first `name(` text. That is not control flow. If someone deletes the `return;` after the opener, the form opens the confirm AND saves at once, and both 4.3 and 4.4 still pass. Check 4.3's label claims that 'each asks before it saves'; a one-line regression makes that false while the check stays green.
evidence: `asksFirst` returns `f.handler.indexOf(opener) < min(f.handler.indexOf(name + "("))`. In src/app/admin/config/config-form.tsx:97-101 the code is `if (changed) { setConfirmFd(fd); return; } runSave(fd);`. Delete `return;` (line 99): `setConfirmFd(fd)` still comes before `runSave(`, so `asksFirst` is true, and the form still reaches `runSave`, so 4.4 passes too. A fee-model change, which reprices every future poll, would then save on Save or Enter before the officer answers the confirm. src/app/admin/updown/updown-controls.tsx:1104 `if (simulated) { setConfirmOpen(true); return; }` has the same hole: the simulated feed would be saved without asking. No plant drops the `return`.
fix: Make `asksFirst` structural. In the onSubmit's syntax tree, find the opener `CallExpression`. Require that it sits in the then-block of an `IfStatement` and that this block ends in a `ReturnStatement`. Require that every call to a reached function lies after that `IfStatement`, never inside its then-block. Add two plants, both expecting 4.3: (1) config-form: `L("      setConfirmFd(fd);", "      return;")` becomes `"      setConfirmFd(fd);"` (anchor unique); (2) updown-controls: `"if (simulated) { setConfirmOpen(true); return; }"` becomes `"if (simulated) { setConfirmOpen(true); }"` (unique).

where: scripts/implicit-submit.test.mts §4 census: `reach` / `targetsOf` and the form scan in `censusOfFile`
problem: 4.3 only catches a submit that reaches the confirm's own local function. Two cases slip past it: a form submit that calls the same server action directly, and a form whose `action={fn}` prop commits.
evidence: `reach()` and `targetsOf()` follow only callees bound to local functions; `fnOf(bindingOf(...))` is null for imports. `censusOfFile` reads only the `onSubmit` attribute. Example: in AssignRoleForm, rewrite `setConfirming(true);` (src/app/admin/staff/staff-forms.tsx:196) as `start(async () => { await runAdminAction(() => setStaffRoleAction(new FormData())); });`. Enter now changes a role with no confirm, and 4.3 stays green. A `<form action={save}>` beside `<ConfirmModal onConfirm={save}>` is never read at all.
fix: Also count as a confirm target every imported callee that its target reaches, when the callee comes from a module whose first statement is "use server" (for example `setStaffRoleAction`, `updateGlobalConfigAction`, `updateReadingMethodAction`). Fail any form submit that reaches one of these; the ledger still exempts its two forms. Read `action={identifier|arrow}` the same way as `onSubmit`. Confirm the real tree gains no new hits. Plant the AssignRoleForm rewrite above, using the anchor `"focusFirstInvalid(assignFormRef.current, fields); return; }" + NL + "    setConfirming(true);"`, expecting 4.3.

problem: Only `.requestSubmit()` and `.submit()` count as submitting a form. A confirm that clicks a real submit button (`saveRef.current?.click()`) or dispatches a submit event is not seen as submitting, so 4.1 never asks for `submitsForm`. Yet that real submit button is exactly what Enter presses in that form.
evidence: `SUBMIT_CALLS = new Set(["requestSubmit", "submit"])`, and the fixtures test only those two. The repo already uses the click-a-ref idiom: src/app/admin/ai-usage/cycle-controls.tsx:249 `onSave={() => saveRef.current?.click()}`. In credit-controls.tsx, `saveRef` is bound (line 24) to the form's `type="submit"` Save (line 59).
fix: Treat these as submissions: `.click()` on an identifier or ref bound in the same file to a submit-capable element (`type="submit"`, or a button or kit Button with no type), and `.dispatchEvent(new Event("submit", ...))`. Add a fixture for each. Plant: credit-controls `"        onConfirm={onReset}"` becomes `"        onConfirm={() => saveRef.current?.click()}"`, expecting 4.1.

where: scripts/qa-implicit-submit.mjs (Chromium only) versus the WebKit and Firefox legs in §2
problem: The hidden second text field exists only for WebKit (every iPhone browser), but no real-browser case ever runs WebKit or Firefox. Those legs rest entirely on the hand-written `enterSubmits()` model. The plant 'the second text field dropped' is caught only by that model.
evidence: The drive imports only `chromium`. C:/Users/Ali/AppData/Local/ms-playwright holds chromium-1217 and chromium-1228 and no WebKit or Firefox build, so the drive could not run them as written. I checked the model against each engine's main source: WebKit `HTMLFormElement::submitImplicitly` and `HTMLInputElement::canTriggerImplicitSubmission() { return isTextField(); }`, Firefox `HTMLInputElement::MaybeSubmitForm`, and Chromium `SubmitImplicitly`. It matches them today, but that is a reading of source, not a browser run.

where: scripts/qa-implicit-submit.mjs: case order C1, then C2, then P2, and the header's red-control claim
problem: On the pre-A8j tree, C1 closes the demo account. C2 and P2 then fail as 'the case could not run', never by their own checks. So the header's claim that C2 fails on the old tree via `?reason=close_confirm_required` is never exercised, and P2's old-tree control is hidden behind C1's.
evidence: `closeAccountAction` (src/app/profile/account/actions.ts:89-101) closes the user and the wallet and signs the player out. `/auth/demo`'s `ensureDemoUser` (src/app/auth/demo/route.ts:186-247) resets only the balance and the email, never status or `closedAt`, and the drive does not re-bootstrap anyway. `fresh()` and `asleep()` then wait 90 s for `input[name=confirm]` and throw.
fix: Run C2 first: on the old tree it only bounces back with `?reason=` and closes nothing. Then run C1, then P2. State in the header that P2's old-tree result is hidden by C1's closure. Alternatively, call `signedIn()` at the start of each close-account case and print 'SKIPPED: the account was closed by an earlier case' instead of a FAIL under that case's name.

where: scripts/qa-implicit-submit.mjs: the URL checks in W1, D1 and C1
problem: In three cases, the 'nothing was sent' check misses a submit that the server refused. W1 only checks for `withdrawal=`. D1 and C1 only compare the pathname. D1's balance check proves nothing for a refused deposit, because a refused deposit never moves the balance and keeps the same pathname.
evidence: `withdrawAction` sends refusals to `/wallet/withdraw?error=...` (src/app/wallet/withdraw/actions.ts:70-124). `depositAction` sends them to `/wallet/deposit?error=...` (src/app/wallet/deposit/actions.ts:62). `closeAccountAction` sends them to `/profile/account?reason=...` (src/app/profile/account/actions.ts:94, 99). W2 and C2 already test the query string for `error=` and `reason=`; W1, D1 and C1 do not.
fix: Use the same shape W2 and C2 already use. W1: `!/[?&](withdrawal|error)=/.test(url)`. D1: `!/[?&](deposited|error)=/.test(url)` on the full URL. C1: require that the query string has no `reason=`.

problem: `fresh()` swallows its 90 s 'the guard listens' wait with `.catch(() => {})`. If the page never hydrates, W1, D1, C1 and W3 silently become before-hydration cases and fail with `open:false`, which looks exactly like a regression. BASE also accepts 127.0.0.1, where the repo's own notes say `next dev` never hydrates.
evidence: `fresh()` calls `page.waitForFunction(..., null, { timeout: 90000 }).catch(() => {})`. The BASE regex allows `(localhost|127[.]0[.]0[.]1)`.
fix: Make `fresh()` throw 'the page never woke (the form guard did not start listening)', so `runCase` reports the real cause. Refuse 127.0.0.1 in the BASE guard, or warn that it never hydrates.

problem: Several properties have a check but no plant proving the check can see them: the tabIndex and aria-hidden on the additions (2.3); the `stop()` in the effect's cleanup (3.3); the CLASSIC branch's `guard.confirm` (3.1 only plants the held-open branch); the order inside `requestOpen` (3.2); and 4.1's by-name 'missing' path. Every consumer plant removes the prop; none makes the census stop seeing a real submit.

All five consumer plants delete `submitsForm`, so 4.1 fails through `unguarded`, never through `missing`.
fix: Add these plants (anchors unique in the edited files): (1) CD: `"disabled={!listening} tabIndex={-1} aria-hidden />"` becomes `"disabled={!listening} aria-hidden />"`, expect 2.3. (2) CD: `"      stop();" + NL + "      setListening(false);"` becomes `"      setListening(false);"`, expect 3.3. (3) CD: `"            setOpen(false);" + NL + "            guard.confirm(onConfirm);"` becomes `"            setOpen(false);" + NL + "            onConfirm();"`, expect 3.1. (4) CD: `"    if (openGuard && !openGuard()) return;" + NL + "    onOpen?.();"` becomes the same two lines swapped, expect 3.2. (5) WITHDRAW: `"    form.requestSubmit();"` becomes `"    HTMLFormElement.prototype.requestSubmit.call(form);"`. That is a real submit the census cannot read, so it should be caught as 'missing by name' under 4.1.

where: scripts/implicit-submit.test.mts: the red loop that runs each plant
problem: If a plant breaks the build of confirm-dialog.tsx, every §1 and §2 check fails. Any plant expecting a 1.x or 2.x failure then reads PROVED for the wrong reason, and nothing asserts that the planted module still built. Two other paths rest on in-process checks only (1.2 and 3.1): deposit, whose form is now newly guarded, and the classic branch (`setOpen(false)` then `requestSubmit` through the guard), which is close-account's path.
